scenes.title: A capability without a decision
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize a working tool leaving its problem unsolved Look for the obstacle between ability and improvement
scenes.composition: A working medical device sits in a clinic missing an essential service
addOrChange: Remove heat spectacle and show one dry sink or delayed supply.

cues.narration: A technology can work perfectly while the problem it was meant to solve remains.
cues.visualAction: The device works while the missing service prevents care.

cues.narration: What We Still Have to Solve investigates the obstacles between capability and a better world.
cues.visualAction: Widen to the clinic’s practical dependencies.

scenes.title: When technology works
scenes.viewerPurpose: Ask who can make a useful change happen See why different problems need different kinds of progress
scenes.composition: A ready power installation needs a connection and a decision
addOrChange: Remove cost counters and extra panels, retaining a concrete approval step.

cues.narration: It looks at energy, health, and AI alongside a familiar question: who can make things happen?
cues.visualAction: Planner, crew and household face the stalled connection.

cues.narration: Some challenges need new science; others need institutions capable of learning from what already works.
cues.visualAction: Keep working technology beside the organizational step still missing.

scenes.title: The next bottleneck
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice a lesson from aviation near misses Picture better tools inside an organization unable to admit mistakes
scenes.composition: A near-miss record prompts a discussion of organizational learning
addOrChange: Replace desalination tutorial with incident report, reviewer and maintenance item, without a crash.

cues.narration: A near miss in aviation becomes a clue to how civilization might handle its own mistakes.
cues.visualAction: Open the incident record beside the small procedure change it prompted.

cues.narration: What happens when powerful tools meet organizations that cannot admit something has gone wrong?
cues.visualAction: Show a comparable warning set aside while another system continues running.

scenes.title: A future we can revise
scenes.viewerPurpose: Want to find the point where progress gets stuck Ask where one useful step could begin
scenes.composition: An affected person and operator locate one bottleneck
addOrChange: Keep a single route from observation to possible change, not a complete remedy.

cues.narration: The book invites you to follow a frightening problem down to the place where progress gets stuck.
cues.visualAction: Follow the difficulty to the decision where progress stops.

cues.narration: Where would a useful next step begin?
cues.visualAction: Place a proposed next test beside that decision, leaving the result open.
